text:
Anya: Quick check — wiring up OIDC-based token exchange for a Node client running on GKE (Workload Identity). When we mint a JWT and hit the token exchange endpoint we get 403 with an "aud mismatch" message. Anyone seen this with the SDK or WI flows? Minimal JWT payload below.

Sam: Hey — 99% chance it's the aud. For Workload Identity / STS exchanges the aud must be the STS token endpoint URL (e.g. `https://sts.redwood.example/token`). Our SDK helper `oidcClient.exchange()` expects that by default. Also make sure `iss` is the service account email.

Mike: Also check the GKE annotation on the pod: `iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account: redwood-sa@proj.iam.gserviceaccount.com`. If that mapping is wrong the token won't be accepted.

Anya: Ah — our JWT aud was set to `redwood-client`. Will that definitely fail if not the STS URL? We're using the SDK default helper so thought it might be okay.

Sam: Yup that'll fail. Two quick fixes: (1) set `aud` in the signed JWT to `https://sts.redwood.example/token`, or (2) pass an explicit `audience` param into `oidcClient.exchange({ audience: 'https://sts.redwood.example/token' })`.

Sasha: On Node I solved this with a tiny snippet — works reliably: 
```js
const payload = {
  sub: 'redwood-sa@proj.iam.gserviceaccount.com',
  iss: 'redwood-sa@proj.iam.gserviceaccount.com',
  aud: 'https://sts.redwood.example/token',
  exp: Math.floor(Date.now()/1000) + 300
}
const jwt = sign(payload, privateKey)
await oidcClient.exchange({ jwt, audience: payload.aud })
```
Also double-check `sub` format (email vs numeric ID) depending on your provider.

Anya: Thanks — will swap the aud and try. One more: if STS returns 429, what's our retry stance? exponential with jitter? :thinking_face: 

Sam: Yes — treat 429/5xx with exponential backoff + jitter, cap ~32s. SDK has built-in retries but you can override with `retryConfig`.

devex-bot: Pinned doc: https://internal.redwood.dev/devex/oidc-exchange (contains example configs + aud notes) :link:

Mike: If you still get 403 after changing aud, paste the raw JWT (header.payload) here and I can decode/inspect quickly.

Anya: Will do, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
